title: Paper account waits; two book evaluations fail their quote-age checks
body_html:
Paper account waits; two book evaluations fail their quote-age checks

Paper trading · 2026-11-27T17:00:11.080608-05:00

By the 2026-11-27 22:00:11 UTC cutoff, the paper decision was NO_ACTION and a deliberate wait. It listed no proposals, so no deterministic risk approval or rejection is recorded. The decision refers to a $50 SNDK purchase filled on November 23, but the supplied context does not label that earlier fill as broker or simulated; no current-day fill is recorded. Two active book evaluations failed because their required quotes were too old for a 900-second limit. Their failures are not waits. Book cutoff marks use separate observed bid/ask midpoints from about 18:00 UTC on November 27, before the cutoff; these after-hours marks are not live prices or guaranteed closing prices.

Today's lesson: A marked loss is not a sale

A snapshot loss is not automatically a realized loss. For SNDK, the recorded price of $85.40 was $2.688 below the $88.088 average purchase price. Multiplying that difference by 0.567601 shares gives about a $1.53 unrealized loss, matching the supplied record. The shares were still held in the snapshot.

Portfolio review

Paper account

At the 2026-11-27 22:00:10 UTC account snapshot, the paper account showed $1,949.99 cash and $1,998.46 equity. Its latest performance record, captured earlier at 20:15:25 UTC, reported session P&L of +$6.61 and +0.331866%; that is a separate earlier snapshot, not the account's cutoff equity. The daily decision was NO_ACTION, classified as a deliberate wait: it said the small SNDK position already expressed the supported thesis and the case for adding did not outweigh the uncertainty. The record lists no proposals, so no deterministic risk approval or rejection is reported; no current-day order submission or fill is recorded. The decision record says no open orders were represented. Its strongest counterargument to waiting is that most of the account remained in cash while the recorded SNDK cash-generation baseline looked substantial; the same record cautions that this depends on unusually strong, pricing-sensitive profitability. The account and holding figures are recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.

SNDK — Paper account

The paper snapshot at 2026-11-27 22:00:10 UTC shows 0.567601 SNDK shares, an average purchase price of $88.088, a snapshot price of $85.40, and a market value of $48.47. The recorded unrealized loss is $1.53. For a simple check: ($85.40 − $88.088) × 0.567601 is about −$1.53. This is a snapshot, not a guaranteed closing price. The recorded thesis argues that reported cash generation may be more durable than the market assumes; the daily decision cites $17.546 billion of operating cash flow less $0.181 billion of physical PP&E purchases. Its strongest counterargument is that profitability is exceptional and pricing-sensitive: the decision notes weak NAND pricing outlook, and the thesis warns that margins could normalize sharply. The daily decision was NO_ACTION because the existing small holding already represented the thesis and the record did not establish better incremental risk/reward. It named the next quarterly results as the reassessment point. No current-day proposal or fill is recorded. The decision record refers to a $50 SNDK purchase filled on November 23, but this context does not label that earlier fill as broker or simulated.

Why the paper decision waited

The decision record says the SNDK thesis rests on reported cash generation, while warning that exceptional profitability may fall if NAND pricing weakens. It gives one example calculation: $17.546 billion operating cash flow minus $0.181 billion physical PP&E purchases equals $17.365 billion. That is a historical measure, not a promise of future cash or a complete measure of reinvestment. The same record says pricing drove a large share of earlier revenue growth, which is a direct counterargument to assuming current profitability will last.

Two different quote checks

The run summary records two evaluation failures: mean-reversion could not price MU, and short-horizon could not price SPCX, because each required quote was 8,355 seconds old, beyond the 900-second cap. The book holdings also have admitted cutoff valuation observations at 18:00 UTC under a separate, longer valuation age allowance. Those observations support the stated cutoff marks; they do not erase the failed evaluations.

What to watch next

The recorded SNDK reassessment point is the next quarterly results release, where the decision says to compare cash generation, physical PP&E purchases, profitability, and pricing or volume developments with the thesis. No release date is supplied. The two failed book evaluations remain failures in this report; no completed decisions or fills are supplied for them.

Unrealized P&L: A gain or loss on a holding that has not been sold, based on its recorded valuation.

Mark: A recorded estimate of holdings' value using the prices and times specified in the record; it is not necessarily a live or closing price.

Deterministic risk check: A rule-based check that decides whether a proposed trade meets recorded risk limits. No proposal means there is no approval or rejection to report.

Data timing and limitations

Prices come from recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.
Paper account holdings use the latest recorded snapshot, which may precede fills.
Book marks use observed bid/ask midpoints at price_as_of, not guaranteed live prices. Without an admitted quote the value remains unknown; book gains exclude fees.
Work starting after the cutoff is outside this report. Failures remain labelled.
